utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Could you please call the case, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we resume the cross-examination of the witness Mr. Karavelic, I would like to deal with two issues that will not take much time. First of all, how much time will the Defence still have? The time the witness spent on marking, during the break, is not time used in court by the Prosecution. However, the time used for marking in court will be counted normally. As the Prosecution might have noticed, if the Defence has received a pre-marked map prior to the audience, they are in a position to study them thoroughly and see what markings are made on a map. If, however, markings are made and if in court they are for the first time confronted with these markings, then the Defence is able to follow what the markings are about at the moment they are made. So this enables the Defence to analyse what it is all about. Because they have had no opportunity to analyse any markings prior to the hearing. So what we did, as a matter of fact, is we started a couple of markings in court so that we could all see what it was about, and then once knowing that to continue with the other maps, because we then had an idea what to look at specifically and it was by this way that we could, for example, identify a few inconsistencies in the marking, et cetera, et cetera. So the difference is whether a premarked map has been presented to the Defence and whether the markings have been the subject of study of the Defence. If not, then we -- the Chamber usually prefers to have the marking done in the presence of both the Chamber and the parties. But even there, once we knew what it was about, we allowed further marking to be done during the break. As far as the time is concerned, the Prosecution took three hours and 54 minutes. Until now, the Defence took one hour and 34 minutes. So that would come down to two hours and 20 minutes, I would say. Some of the interventions were not always of such character that a bit less than two hours and 20 minutes would be fair as a remaining time. That is the issue about the time. Then we have still some documents that we have to take decision upon. The first is a document which was tendered by the Prosecution during the -- at the end of the testimony of Mr. Van Baal. The issue was whether the Chamber would ask the Prosecution also to refrain from tendering the document. The Prosecution has explained to us that since there was something attached to the document, that that would not do well. Madam Registrar it was I think P2380. Yes. We will not ask the Prosecution to refrain from tendering; therefore, it is admitted into evidence. Then we still have some documents of which Madam Registrar would like to invite you -- do we have to do that in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I explained the difference to you in view of P2380. The document we asked you not to tender, well you finally decided what you would not tender, was a statement of a witness, which, at least the part presented, has been fully read, nothing attached to it. And that is the difference with the document the Prosecution tendered in respect of Mr. Van Baal. Mr. Ierace, do we need any further documents to be tendered that have been used during the testimony of Mr. Philipps or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, firstly, in relation to the chart that was filed, so I presume that you do not require that to be formally tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The chart, you mean the big chart?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think most of us received -- do we -- Madam Registrar, do you have a copy of the big chart?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We do not have a copy as an exhibit. I don't think it's specifically mentioned in the report -- no, it's mentioned, but we have some who have received reports with a copy of the big chart with all the, I would say, the faceless people on it, and some of us have not received it. So there might be some confusion. If you say it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise for that most sincerely. I had assumed that Your Honours had a copy of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most of the Judges had.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I certainly have copies now, which I would make available for tendering and for distribution to you. So that would be Exhibit P3726 for the English version, and 3726.1 for the B/C/S version. In relation to the documents that I showed the witness during re-examination, I think the relevant parts of those documents have been elicited orally, so I don't seek to tender them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I am wondering whether the computerised version is also tendered. It would --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am of two minds about that. The computerised version is nothing more than slides of details of the chart. There is nothing added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I know that. One of the advantages is that when you are sitting behind your desk, either you cover your whole computer with a map, if you want to look at it, or you use your screen. But, perhaps if you would say it would be available, even if it would not be tendered, but copies would be available just for practical purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We have hard copies, if you wish it, Mr. President, in other words, a pile of A-4 paper-size hard copies of what was on the screen. If you prefer it in CD form --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is another option, or in CD form.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, that would require the relative software. I think it is PowerPoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is PowerPoint. It is general software.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So whichever you prefer, Mr. President, we can provide if you want it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll let you know. My preference is certainly the CD-ROM. I can't imagine that we'd ask you for both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That would be no problem, Mr. President. At some convenient point, Mr. President, can I take 15 seconds of your time to say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would first like to deal with any other documents. I do see that the Prosecution has not tendered anything, but the Defence did, in respect of Mr. Philipps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in view of the chart which shows the structure of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, the Defence has an objection to accepting this into evidence, because after the cross-examination we did not receive answers to the relevant questions, and we would like to emphasise that the structure which is presented here is not in accordance with the actual situation which at the time was enforcing the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. Specifically, we saw that the chart presents the tactical group Vogosca in an incorrect way. And in view of the evidence presented by the Defence, D42, as well as Prosecution exhibits, this was a document presented by the Prosecution to Mr. Philipps. So, on the basis of these two documents, it could be concluded that the Vogosca tactical group did not include the Ilidza Brigade. When asking questions about the mixed anti-tank artillery regiment and the 4th Engineering Regiment, we saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, let's not discuss the -- you are talking about whether this chart finally would reflect the absolute truth. That is not a question of admissibility. The chart reflects what the expert has concluded on the basis of the documents he has studied and inspected. And of course, if there is anything you would like to present or already have presented which would put into doubt what the expert has told us, you are entirely free to do so. But the consequence of your position would be that whenever a witness is contradicted by another witness, his testimony would not be admissible evidence any more. It is, I think, not a matter of admissibility you are addressing at this moment, apart from your claim that what is on your papers is the full truth. I do not know that. I think the Chamber doesn't know that. We first have to deliberate on all the evidence presented to us. Any other objections against the chart?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I just must emphasise that the Defence so far did not receive the documents used by Mr. Philipps in order to develop the diagram, except for a letter from Mr. Ierace which noted the ERN numbers, and we received copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The report filed in respect of Mr. Philipps contained a 60-page list of references for each aspect of the chart. In respect of some of those entries, a letter which accompanied the report and was filed with it indicated that further references would be provided at a later date. On the 30th of May, some 13 days later, that further collection of references was provided both to the Defence and to the Trial Chamber, and it comprised an additional approximately 24 pages. Prior to the original filing on the 17th of May, I raised with the Trial Chamber a question of whether the Prosecution should file a copy of each of the documents from which the chart was composed. The Trial Chamber ruled that the Prosecution should not file the documents, but if during Mr. Philipps' evidence he was taken to any of the documents, then those documents could be tendered. That ruling was on the basis that all of the material upon which he relied had either been disclosed to the Defence from the Prosecution or from the Defence to the Prosecution. During the course of Mr. Philipps' evidence, my learned colleagues pointed out that the documents they had disclosed to the Prosecution were, of course, without ERN numbers because that doesn't happen. ERN numbers are not allocated until they are submitted to the Evidence Unit. I am more than happy to provide the Defence with a list of the relevant ERN numbers for the documents they have disclosed to us so as to facilitate any further use of those documents by the Defence, and indeed should we get so far, in the Defence case. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, the matter has been discussed thoroughly during the examination, also your difficulties in retrieving the documents. I then told the parties that if you needed specific documents, you could ask the Prosecution, give a list of those documents you needed. I didn't hear from you anymore in respect of those documents. So that is a matter that we have dealt with. Yes. So, if there is no -- if there is not any further objection, the chart is admitted into evidence. And then, Madam Registrar. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D142, B/C/S document dated 07/7/1993 signed by General Stanislav Galic. D142.1, partial translation of D142.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as the translation, the partial characteristic of the translation is concerned, does that raise any further issues, Mr. Ierace, because that is one of the things you mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then they are admitted into evidence. Just for the sake of the record, we earlier talked about PT2380 used during the testimony of Mr. Van Baal, that is admitted under seal. Yes, then you asked for 15 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Fifteen seconds, Mr. President, and counting. At the end of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this something new or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. If I may have the leave. The booth told me that they didn't catch one of the exhibit numbers. If you could repeat it so it is entered into the French transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, but now I change to the English channel and would like to know where I find it. Yes. The document tendered in relation of -- to Mr. Van Baal was P2380. The chart related to the testimony of Mr. Philipps was P3726, and the same number but then dot one added. And the Defence documents were D142, D142.1. If we have heard all the numbers, we will then give Mr. Ierace an opportunity to spend 15 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at the conclusion of the evidence of this witness, might I respond to what could be called the Hungarian translation issue, and secondly, might I update the Trial Chamber in relation to the Prosecution timetable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may do so, and we will then first resume the cross-examination of Mr. Karavelic. Madam Usher, can you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, General Karavelic. May I again remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. Now your cross-examination will be resumed. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karavelic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, yesterday when I asked you a question about your knowledge about the number of snipers that the BH army had at their disposal, you said that you did not hear about the data given to you by the Defence that was quoted in Mr. Siber's book. Could you perhaps tell us in which units did BH army have snipers?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, according to the establishment of the army, the BH army had -- in each of their firing section, they should have had a sniper. However, I can only judge this by the 1st Corps of the BH army, that the number of snipers was not really well represented within that unit. How many snipers the 1st Corps had, this information could be -- it is possible to get it through the -- from the archive.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you please answer whether the snipers were under the control of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer such a question. You would have to understand what a formation -- what establishment is. I think I answered in the previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, my question was whether snipers were under the control of the 1st Corps. Did the 1st Corps issue orders in relation to snipers?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any firing section, according to the establishment, should have a sniper. The 1st Corps had the minimum number of snipers. That is the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show Mr. Karavelic a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please assist, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is 146.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my learned colleague handed me a bundle of documents this morning. Might she indicate -- thank you. Or perhaps she might indicate if this document which I have just been handed is one from the bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is one from the bundle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just ask you if I may just have one copy and then I will return it. I see there are not enough copies for everyone. Just so that the witness -- I can show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, is this a document dated 12th of December, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document, which is an order, says: "According to the order of command of the 1st Corps number 5 through 7, 5 through 8, dated 12th of December, 1993, in relation to the regrouping of snipers. In order to resist the aggressor, I hereby order, and in order to prepare the manpower, I hereby order." And then we have various items, four items, from which we can see that the order is in relation to carrying out an order of the 1st Corps. Could you perhaps confirm through this document that snipers were, indeed, under the control, under direct command of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every now and then, depending on the combat situation in Sarajevo, there were probably -- there was probably regrouping of forces, and, among other things, from this document you can see that there were sniping groups that were created. And according to the combat rules, it is possible to do this in order to prevent possible breakthroughs into Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you answer whether within brigades -- specifically we are talking about 1993. Do you have any knowledge whether sniper -- sniping platoons were established within battalion of some brigades?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All commanders on all levels have the right to do any kind of regrouping of units within their own formation, within their own unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you please tell us, and we are still talking about 1993, do you have any knowledge where and which location were located -- were sniping platoons located? I am going to ask you specifically about the sniping platoon, its location, the sniping platoon of the 1st Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that the sniping platoon was located in the school Blagoje Panevic near Cenex, can you please confirm this fact?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this corps was used only in the beginning; after that, I don't think it was used.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like Mr. Karavelic shown Document Number 147.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you see before you the document, which in the left corner says, "Commander of the 1st Motorised Brigade 2nd of October, 1993," and it is in the form of an order

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On page 2 of this document you have the signature of commander Ramiz Velic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, is it correct that through this -- that this order enables it to -- makes it possible for the sniping platoon to be established within the 1st and 2nd and 3rd battalion?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel perhaps repeat her -- could the counsel please repeat -- the booths have not been given the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have additional documents for the booth? If not, could you then please repeat, Ms. Pilipovic, please repeat, but what exactly -- the question, I take it. Could you please repeat the question. I see that the booth are now provided with copies of the document. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, in this order, does it say that the sniper platoon is to be created, is to be composed from the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Motorised Battalion?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Does the -- under item three of this order, does it say, "The sniper platoon is to be placed in the former school Blagoje Parovic"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you answer whether during the conflict in Sarajevo, were there other schools that the BH army used in order to place troops and weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard -- the question contains the words "were there other schools." The item the question follows on from related to a former school. Perhaps my friend could clarify whether she means other former schools or buildings being currently used as schools.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The document talks about former schools. Ms. Pilipovic, were you referring to school buildings not functioning as schools, or could you please clarify the issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was talking about former buildings which in 1992, 1993, and 1994, were buildings where -- which were used as schools at that relevant time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but Ms. Pilipovic, if you are asking about were there other schools, then at least it should follow from this document that a school was used and not a former school. I thought you might refer to the building, but if you say -- I do understand by "a former school" that a building which is at the relevant time not used for teaching purposes but before was used for that aim. I think we should be very clear on this. Please proceed, and please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you tell us, in the period 1992, 1993, and 1994, were buildings that before the conflict were schools, were these buildings used for the accommodation of BH army soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps in a very small percentage, although with the observation that the schools throughout the war in Sarajevo were not able to function. These were only buildings, facilities. They should not be called schools. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. There were burnt buildings without windows, without glass in windows. These were not schools.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, the Defence would like to show you a document, D97, which is a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And the Defence has copied this document in a sufficient number of copies. D97.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, do you see a document before you where in the left-hand corner, top left-hand corner, you can see the command of the 102nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the document on line two, it says: "Please through the Ministry allow priorities for the factory of wire, Valter Peric facility and primary school Slobodan Vukovic, Petar Dakic, Marsal Tito Barracks, Energoinvest building, kindergarten the 8th of March, school Pavle Goranin and hotel Zagreb." Could you confirm that this document is correct and that these were the facilities that the army, that is the 102 Motorised Brigade, used as facilities for accommodation?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this document has been taken from the archive of the BH army, then that is what it says, that is it. I have no reason to doubt it. This just means that it is confirmed that this was asked for, and in numerous cases, there were many examples that I personally asked permission from the government and I cannot understand what the government would be, what kind of government would that be if they allow troops to go into school which is functioning. That just wouldn't be normal.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, Mr. Karavelic, whether the snipers of BH army operated from snipers' nests?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me something else. The 1st Corps of the BH army had 74.000 people, 75.000 people. We had what we had and we defended ourselves. We used everything that was at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, I asked you if the facilities in Sarajevo in the part of the city which was under the control of the BH army, do you have any knowledge that the facilities were used as snipers' nests?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many kinds of nests. This is used in military terminology. And if there were snipers and they existed, it is -- I cannot rule out the possibility that there were such nests.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us which facilities you know of that the BH army used as snipers' nests?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire defence line around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that the facilities of the refrigerator, the Bristol building, the Executive Council, the engineering faculty, the Electro-Technical building, that these were building that were used, among others, that were used as snipers' nests?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All buildings that were high-rise flats were avoided because they were at the risk of being fired on by the other side with the tanks and other things. So if they operated, it was always from the lowest possible levels where there was minimum possibility of them being seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like the witness to be shown the document 148.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the interpreters have a copy, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we distribute copies to the interpreters' booth as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, but there are not enough copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that once the Prosecution has identified the document, if it is in the bundle, that they would give their copy to the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President. The transcript doesn't record the full exhibit number. Might I have that again. 148 is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is 148.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you see the document before you of the 102nd Motorised Brigade dated 18th of September, 1993? Is that an order where under item 1 it says that the facilities of Halnica [phoen] is exclusively to be used for snipers' nests, observation points, firing position of certain weapons?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karavelic. Mr. Karavelic, in your statement you spoke of the order of battle of the brigades and you said that every brigade on the front line had one battalion, one reserve, and then one having a rest. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, what was the depth of the brigade order of battle when we are bearing in mind all of the elements of the order of battle from the front line until the reserve, that is also including units that were being -- that were having a rest?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want the real situation, what really happened, or do you want how it should have been done, according to the rules of using the units?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us: 1992, 1993, 1994, what was the depth --

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Motorised Brigade has the depth -- according to the rule, a Motorised Brigade should have a depth of 3 to 5 kilometres from the front line to the rear. I believe that's the figures. That is according to the rules. And from that, everything else can be concluded in relation to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you tell us: The brigades that you marked on the map, how many battalions did they comprise at -- would you be able to locate them?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On average, depending on what kind of brigade we are talking about, whether it is a mountain, infantry, motorised brigade, or mechanised brigade, on average a brigade would have three to six battalions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you perhaps show us on the map that you used, and I believe that map number is 3644, Prosecution map, where you marked all the command posts of the brigades. Would you be able to mark the command posts of the battalions?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had three brains, I would not be able to do this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you, as the commander, as the corps commander, were you supposed to know all the command posts of your battalions?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Do you know that I had 30 brigades times five or six battalions? Do you know how many command posts that would mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us such a number, large number of battalions, where -- where were they, in which buildings were they accommodated, were they billeted? Where were the --

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rule was that the command of the brigades were -- according to the scheme, as I have told you, that is how they were located while the commands of the battalions were in the immediate vicinity, that is just behind front line. That is how they had to be located. And this is most frequently -- was most frequently the case, that the commander of the battalions were there during the -- because of the rotation. When there was a rotation, then they would be moved. There would be a new command -- battalion command that would come take over the line, the position, and then they would move.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us which buildings were used for the billeting?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 99 per cent of the cases, anything that was destroyed, burnt out, it would then be slightly adapted, modified, and then cellars in such facilities which could not be used for anything at all, not even for soldiers, they were, however, used.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you told us speaking of weapons, that you did not have many weapons and that the artillery was outside of the city?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in Sarajevo you had one tank that was working and one that was not functioning, I believe?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Except there was a third tank which was never used at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you to slow a bit down. I see that -- I hear that the interpreters are out of breath almost. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the tanks that you mentioned, did you have other artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Howitzers, 105 millimetres, and mortars, 120. That depends on -- some people believe that -- place them as artillery and some as infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where were they located.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Howitzer, 105 millimeters, I showed it yesterday on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show Mr. Karavelic, I believe the document is 149.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, can you please assist. If there are not sufficient copies for the booth, then I would like to ask Ms. Pilipovic to quote only slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you see before you a document of the command of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one document dated --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Dated 16th of February, 1992 -- 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read under item one after "I order."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under one it says: "The spent mixed artillery rocket brigade of the 1st Sarajevo Corps and organisational units are to be disposed in other war units, according to the following schedules."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, is it true, according to this order, that the 3rd Motorised Brigade received a 120-millimetre mortar battery with all materiel and assets?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where your 3rd Motorised Brigade was on the 16th and what its zone of responsibility was, which parts of the city was it responsible for?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Motorised Brigade, I think it was -- its duties were taken over by the 102nd Motorised Brigade and its zone is the Azici Stupska Petlya area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, is it true that according to this order, the Howitzer battery of 105 millimetres was placed in the 101st Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some things were crossed out here, but it does seem to say that the Mechanised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the 1st Motorised Brigade was? Obviously, we are talking about the 1st Motorised Brigade, since the Mechanised Brigade was crossed out.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be mechanised because there was no Motorised Brigade; it never existed in Sarajevo and it's the zone from Kosevo to Zuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did this brigade also cover Buca Potok?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was close to the border with the 2nd Motorised Brigade, so it is possible that it did cover that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did the self-propelled 122 millimetre Howitzer battery, was that allocated to the 6th Motorised Brigade? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where the 6th Motorised Brigade was placed, which parts of the city of Sarajevo was it responsible for?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it only existed in the course of 1992 and it was disbanded. This is February 1993, so that brigade didn't exist anymore. It was disbanded around this time or perhaps slightly before this date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Under item D, we have a Howitzer battery of 122 millimeters which was deployed in the 2nd Motorised Brigade. Did the 2nd Motorised Brigade cover the area of Miasca [phoen], Solika, and Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Alipasino Polje in depth, but the two things you said before, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did say by depth, did it include Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karavelic, when we analyse this document, do you still stand by your statement that the artillery in your -- of your corps was outside of the city?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you tell us whether as part of your corps, you had a mixed artillery battalion?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us as part of the mixed artillery battalion, which weapons did you have at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to refer to the archives of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I think that during the entire period, this battalion -- this artillery battalion had maybe two or three anti-aircraft guns, single barrel, or double barrel ones. And in the beginning, it perhaps had a couple of the 2M Strijela weapons, and nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where the mixed artillery battalion was deployed? Can you tell us its zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its zone of responsibility was the whole of Sarajevo because this was an anti-aircraft defence unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the command post was?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, but I can't say it. I don't know the name and the place. It is a place south of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "south of the corps command," could you be more specific, please?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just below the Grdonj facility.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you tell us whether, as part of the 1st Corps, the anti-armour battalion was also active?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after September 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show document D150 to Mr. Karavelic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, do you have a document from -- in front of you from April, 1994?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And from this document from April 1994, can be conclude that this is an order about assigning to war duties of the 1st Motorised Brigade in the armoured battalion?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, as part of the armoured battalion, can you tell which weapons did the armoured battalion have at its disposal?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, that one single tank or those two tanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any APCs?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later we tried to manufacture a kind of APC. We had a number, a small number, of APCs with wheels. They had rubber tyres, wheels, and these probably were left over from the police. I am not sure exactly where they came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you please tell us where the armoured battalion was deployed?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a part of the 1st Motorised Brigade. This is the brigade that used to be mechanised. It is a brigade from Kosevo Brdo, including Zuc. That was its area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did your artillery operate in the region of the Ozrenska Ulica, in the theological faculty in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to say to this question. I do not wish to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President. I have a difficulty with the question. I think the word missing before faculty was "theological" faculty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I understood, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the evidence thus far is that Ozrenska and the theological faculty in Nedzarici were in areas controlled by the Serb forces. That being the case, I have a difficulty in understanding the question unless my friend means did the 1st Corps artillery target the region of Ozrenska and the theological faculty. So perhaps that might be clarified. I assume from the answer that the witness also has some difficulty with the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but expressed it only, I think, after you were on your feet. On the other hand, even if --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's not true. The witness was giving his answer before I rose to my feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is true, I have to apologise. It is not clear, my recollection. If I made a mistake, I shouldn't have done it. I was just thinking about whether you can ask a question to the witness even if the question is such, although being clear, would go in a different direction from evidence we heard before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I entirely agree, Mr. President, but because it has not been put to any witness earlier that those areas were controlled by the ABiH, it follows that it hasn't been the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I first ask you, Ms. Pilipovic, whether your question was about operations in the area or operations targeting the areas you've just mentioned, Ozrenska and the area of the theological faculty.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my question was: Was the artillery of the 1st Corps operating or active towards Ozrenska and the theological faculty in Nedzarici. Your Honour, the Defence would like to show a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, then I think the issue was caused by the way your question was presented to us. I don't know. It said whether they operated in the region "of" and not "towards." So, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, is this a document of the 101st Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it states in the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the fourth line, does it state that your artillery operated in the zone of Ozrenska and in the zone of the theological faculty in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it states in the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer, from which positions was it active from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: According to the translation accompanying the document, it reads: "Our artillery targeted the zone of reservoir in Ozrenska Street." Perhaps that could again be clarified. We had the same problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is a translation problem or anything else, but Ms. Pilipovic, your question comes to us in English that the fourth line would state that "your artillery operated in the zone of Ozrenska and in the zone of the theological faculty," where the translation you provided says that "our artillery targeted zone of reservoir in Ozrenska Street and in zone of the theology school in the territory." There is again the same difference. I don't know whose mistake it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I will clarify it. Your Honour, It is not a mistake in the translation but I will clarify the question in a way that Mr. Karavelic can answer the following, whether this document states under item two, "information about our forces."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you confirm when we say "our forces" that these are -- that this is the command of the 101st Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As part of item two, under item five, as part of "our" forces. When it says here, "our artillery," do you take that to mean that it is the command of the 101st Mountain Brigade and that we are talking about the artillery as part of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I am not stating it, but this is stated by the commander of this brigade. And when it states here, "our artillery," it's an ambiguous term. It can be the artillery of another brigade which provided support to this brigade. It can be another corps brigade or it can be one that is part of his brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karavelic. This document talks about artillery within the zone of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that cannot be within anybody else's zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karavelic, can you please tell us which position targeted -- from which positions were the Ozrenska and the theology faculty zones targeted?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From which positions?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I would first need to know the answer, whose artillery it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said it was the artillery of the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is all the artillery of the 1st Corps, in the corps, in the brigade and in the division. So I would need to know exactly which one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I am only asking you about the Ozrenska Street and the theology faculty. Which positions were targeting these areas?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not able to answer that question. I am saying again that it is very difficult to respond to such minute details regarding a war that lasted for four years and where there was a lot of firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you are saying that you don't know the artillery positions?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could be anywhere in Sarajevo. I don't wish to defend myself. I just wish to draw your attention to the kind of questions that you are asking. It could be possible that it is from the reservoir, from Mojmilo, from Dobrinja, from Zuc. The commander of the brigade has the right to change the places of his weapons, to rotate the firing positions at any point. And if he had been firing and this had been spotted, and return fire came and it was very strong, perhaps he could have changed these positions. In the course of a day, a mortar could be firing from several positions in the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are questions which, for a soldier, if I may say so without insulting anyone, these are absurd questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, in order to refresh your recollection, if the Defence were to show you a document arising from your order, would you be able to tell us which part of the zone of responsibility did the corps artillery fire in? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence would like to show Mr. Karavelic document 152.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, do you have a document before you which states in the left-hand corner: "Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, command of the 1st Corps, 25th of October, 1993"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And it says, "Order for defence." On the page of that document, 601, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is a document from the archives, I can say -- and if it is not forged, then I can say that yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document was disclosed by the Prosecution to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, do you see on the second page of this order under item 5, doesn't it say, "1st Motorised Brigade is organising the defence in the following zones: Vis, Brijesce, museum, Brotherhood and Unity Bridge on the Miljacka river." This is under item 5.1.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And just below that, before it says 5.2, it says: "Command post is in the area of the gas works." Could you please tell us where that is, where is that on the Sarajevo map, this facility, Plinara, the gas works?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To this very day, I don't know where the gas works is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Under item 5.2, below it says, "Command post is in the area of Kras, 2nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you indicate where that is, please.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This probably refers to the Kras chocolate and biscuit factory, if that is the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us in which part of the city of Sarajevo it is located?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't, believe me. Sarajevo is -- I don't know where the Kras factory is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the third page of this document, under number 5.6, it says -- so item 5.6, it says: "Croatian brigade Kralj Tvrtko is organising a decisive defence in the following zone: Bridge on the Miljacka, Vrbanja bridge, crossroads of Djuro Djakovic Street and Marshal Tito Street," and underneath it says, "Command post in primary school Alija Alijagic." Mr. Karavelic, can you please tell us until what time did the Croatian Kralj Tvrtko Brigade, which was billeted in the Alija Alijagic primary school, operated as part of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of October 25, 1993. Soon after that, this brigade was placed under the command of the 1st Corps. When that brigade was disarmed, and after that or since then it was formed, established, under this name and it was under command of the 1st Corps until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you tell us until what time period did you operate jointly with, let's put it this way, with the Croatian side, the HVO? Until what time was it together with the 1st Corps in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forces of the Croatian Defence Council in the city of Sarajevo, we acted jointly from the beginning until the end, with the remark that up until this date, until this time, maybe a month sooner, earlier or a month later, the forces of the Croatian Defence Council were not under the command of the 1st Corps but were under the command of Mate Boban, Blaskic, and so on, even though they participated in the defence of Sarajevo. But since that time, with the forming of this brigade, according to a decision by the Bosnia-Herzegovina Presidency, it was under the direct command of the 1st Corps until the end of the war. In other parts of the zone of responsibility of the 1st Corps, the HVO was in Vares and Kiseljak, particularly in Kiseljak. It never acted together jointly with the BH army and the 1st Corps, but in Vares, it operated in a similar fashion as it did in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say that in Kiseljak, it did not act as part of the 1st Corps -- and the period of 1993, did the HVO [Realtime transcript read in error "H"] shell Sarajevo from those positions? Did you have any information like that while you were the commander of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, there were all kinds of information and there was information like that. And I can say that on several occasions, I commanded the air force to -- I issued orders for the air force to launch an attack, even though I never had any air force at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. The interpreter apologises. Could the answer of the witness be repeated so that the French booth can get it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were all kind of information, amongst other things; I heard many things. And were I to tell you that I myself, on numerous occasions, commanded the air force to take off in order to protect and defend Sarajevo, but I actually never had any air force or a single airplane, nor the defence of Sarajevo had such forces at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, as commander of the 1st Corps in the period of 1992, 1993, and 1994, can you tell us how joint military groups operated in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information that in 1992, a joint military working group was formed?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not by the command of the 1st Corps. Maybe this refers to the Main Staff, which formed a mobile command group. Is that what you are thinking of?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, I am thinking about the joint group for talks where members of the warring parties, at the level of the Main Staff, took part in negotiations to resolve the situation in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in the work of these joint military work groups?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite often, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I see that it is time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic. Before we adjourn, I first would like to say for the transcript that on page 13, lines 4 and 5, the writing of the name Ramiz Velic with a "V" instead of a "B" could create some confusion, since there was a witness named Velic. But his name was written with a "V" and the document which shows the name writes "Velic" with a "B."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in a similar vein, page 22, line 21, "destroyed" should be "deployed." And might I have a minute or two in the absence of the witness when we resume? It is in relation to a question asked about five questions ago. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we perhaps do that after the break. We will first have the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I saw you were on your feet but you sat down again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I was hoping for the break, Mr. President, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can imagine that we are all very tired, so we will adjourn until -- yes, Mr. Karavelic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I was told yesterday, Your Honours, that I wasn't speaking the truth regarding my detention and stay in Sremska Mitrovica, I have a copy of an original document here. I can also provide the original from Sarajevo about being admitted to the Sremska Mitrovica prison and also my documents about my release from the Sremska Mitrovica prison, and they bear my signature. So if this is necessary, I can provide these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If it will assist the Trial Chamber and if you so desire, if that could be provided to the Prosecution, we are happy to photocopy it and distribute copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness is allowed not to discuss the document with the Prosecution but to give a -- give this document to the Prosecution. Perhaps you give it to the registrar and she will then pass it to the Prosecution. Madam Usher, could you please assist. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, you wanted to raise an issue. But before doing so, might we just go into closed session for a very short period of time. We are not yet in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I direct the attention of the Trial Chamber to a question asked by my learned colleague shortly before the break. At page, I think it is 31, line 25, it is incorrectly indicated as an answer. In fact, it was a question. And it reads as follows: "When you say that in Kiseljak it did not act as part of the 1st Corps in the period of 1993, did the H..." And I interpose, I think that should be HVO, "...shell Sarajevo from those positions? Did you have any information like that while you were the commander of the 1st Corps?" I assume that that is an accurate translation of the question, but I notice my friend is shaking her head. So perhaps we could first clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will check this, but I believe that this was "HVO," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it is appropriate for Ms. Pilipovic to respond since she asked the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree that it is Ms. Pilipovic who will respond; on the other hand, I think she needs the assistance of Mr. Piletta-Zanin, since she can't read English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I assume my reading of the question was translated into B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but we can't check the translation. Mr. Piletta-Zanin can. Ms. Pilipovic, after you have conferred with Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think, in fact, I am sure that my question was whether there was any information or knowledge whether from the positions in Kiseljak HVO was shelling Sarajevo. I cannot follow my entire question the way it was phrased.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That will suffice, Mr. President, for the purposes of my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There was no suggestion in the Defence pre-trial brief that the Defence included the proposition that any shelling in Sarajevo was a consequence of Croatian forces outside Sarajevo. Further, we have heard evidence from a number of senior UN military officials throughout the period covered in the indictment. It has not once been put to them, nor has the proposition been put to any other Prosecution witness, that any of the shelling which is the subject of the indictment originated from Croatian forces in Kiseljak or anywhere else outside Sarajevo or, indeed, inside Sarajevo. It is raised for the first time with two weeks to go in the Prosecution case. In my respectful submission, the Defence should be precluded from exploring that line of potential defence at this stage in those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic. Well, let me first establish that the witness finally did not answer the question. That is at least, for the time being, some relief for you, perhaps, Mr. Ierace. But I think you are very concerned about the future, whether similar questions would come up. Yes. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the question of the Defence the way that it was asked, and this was about the information or knowledge, whether there was -- he did know anything about it, the Defence asked Mr. Karavelic to look at the document where for the first time a Croatian brigade is mentioned. And it was about the definition of the Croatian brigade, which is why I asked the question about the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council. And the witness himself said, "You mean the Croatian Defence Council that was based in Kiseljak"? So my question was in relation to the information that was in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I am not saying that -- and I don't think that Mr. Ierace says that he doesn't understand what could have caused your question. But his complaint is about introducing a, I would say, potential totally new line of defence never indicated before.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the document that was shown to the witness, to Mr. Karavelic, is a document which is an order of the 1st Corps of the BH army and the witness told us within the 1st Corps of the BH army a Croatian brigade Kralj Tvrtoko also operated, was also deployed. So we are talking about after the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I am not saying that we are not talking about the 1st Corps. But I think the complaint of the Prosecution is where you put at an earlier stage that shelling might have been done by the Croatian brigades. I mean, if you would come up tomorrow with --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the point is that the Croatian brigade Kralj Tvrtko operated within the 1st Corps in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you would say shelling by the 1st Corps towards Sarajevo is part of the Defence case. At least it is now clear what your intent is. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Provided there is that understanding, Mr. President, that the question, or rather, I should say, the Defence case rests on shelling by the 1st Corps, I have no complaint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So -- and what Ms. Pilipovic actually did is to identify one unit, I would say, for the 1st Corps, is that what --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That is not the case, Mr. President. The evidence is, from this witness in cross-examination, that there was a Croatian brigade, and that was under the command and control of the 1st Corps from around the time of October 1993. He initially said it was shortly after that date and then later seemed to be saying, it must have been before that date, given the name of the brigade, and the fact of the brigade in this order. He said in relation to the Croatian forces before that time, his words were that, "We acted jointly from beginning to the end," meaning the war. That appears at page 31, line 13. The question which bases my objection and concern was as to whether there was shelling of Sarajevo from Kiseljak, which I understand to be some considerable distance from Sarajevo. That is an entirely different matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. The second issue is not whether there was any shelling from within the city of Sarajevo to the owned positions, to the positions controlled by the 1st Corps, but that the newly introduced element would be that a similar thing would have been from outside Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If I could just clarify that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness made the point that the unity of purpose that operated within Sarajevo between Croatian and Bosniak forces did not apply elsewhere, that is, outside Sarajevo. If required, I can find that reference. So the issue bluntly is: Any suggestion by the Defence at this late stage that shelling in the indictment was attributable to Croatian forces, for whatever reason directing fire from Kiseljak, is simply too late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the clarification given by my -- that my learned colleague asked for, can be -- he can have that from the redirecting examination. That is what I understood, because I think I am having some difficulty in following exactly what my learned colleague said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the concern of Mr. Ierace which could not be dealt with in re-examination is that you are putting questions to this witness which suggest a totally new line of defence, that would mean Croatian forces firing from outside the city of Sarajevo on the positions inside Sarajevo. May I do the following: Whenever you would touch the area of firing by non-Bosnian Serb forces from outside the city, that you would be very careful and that we then at least give Mr. Ierace the opportunity to object to such questions. And then we will hear the question first, then hear the objection, and then we will then decide. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before we resume with the witness, in relation to the issues I foreshadowed this morning, if we don't finish the witness before the end of the day, might I at least reserve the last 15 minutes or so? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I take it that we will --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We should finish this witness by today. Yes. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Karavelic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. meantime, and in order not to waste time, we ask for the original of the document or the copy of the original of the document that was provided by the witness and we are still waiting for the copy of the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I have given a copy to the Registrar. Mr. President, I have another copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that distribution of this document and inspection of the original should not cause considerable problems. Please be seated, Mr. Karavelic. Ms. Pilipovic, you may resume the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, before the break we were speaking of mixed military working groups. Could you perhaps clarify for us whether at the time, that is in 1992, 1993, and 1994, whether there was also a military commission which was in operation, mixed commission, and military mixed groups, or did these working groups part -- were they part of the mixed commission?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that there was a group. I cannot confirm whether this is one or the other thing that you are talking about, to be honest. I cannot remember the documents. For instance, I believe that there were such documents, but I did very frequently take part in these groups, asked by the commander for a couple of hours to go to talks to the airport or nearby, and I very frequently took part in these negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, these talks, which sides, the parties -- which parties did take place? I mean, the Serb side, UNPROFOR, which sides took place?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the time, four sides, the international forces, that is UNPROFOR, BH army, VRS, and the HVO, the Army of Republika Srpska, and the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying to us that these meetings were held on the level of the corps or on the level of the command?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Always on the level of the main commands.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "main commands," you mean the commands of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who was the representative of the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very frequently, it would be Colonel General Tolimir, lieutenant General Tolimir, and I was personally there when there was Cedomir Sladoje -- Sladoje Cedomir, who was Lieutenant General, and there was also security officer from the command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps - I cannot remember his name - was also there once or twice also when General Mladic came for the talks in the course of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you tell us whether at these meetings, whether there were records, minutes kept of these meetings, whether any decisions were made?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps tell us about one of the decisions that were made there?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, the meetings resulted in some decisions, and the decisions were about going through the current situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina political military situation, and very frequently ceasefires and truces and the cessation of hostilities were discussed. And this is specifically, I can tell you that without looking at any document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, did you, as a corps commander, commander of the 1st Corps, did you receive protests from UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what did these protests relate to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many of those protests came in relation to the violation of ceasefires, and there were also protests - again, I cannot tell you how many of them - came on alleged firing of so-called mobile mortars, as UNPROFOR called them, from some locations inside Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally send some protests to UNPROFOR representatives?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean my command? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you send such protests?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I only made protests directing -- directed at the violations of the ceasefire or the violations of cessation of hostilities. Perhaps there were other reasons also.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As commander of the corps, did you also receive casualty reports of civilians in certain incidents in the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you conduct inquiries into such reports?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what you mean, but often, yes, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If you can, could you give us an example?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All investigations regarding any kind of incident were conducted by the Security Service of the general staff. Officers of my security section were also included in those investigations, and everything was done under the auspices of the civilian police. And in certain cases, it was under the jurisdiction of the civilian courts of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you perhaps mention any incident about which you know conduct -- enquiries were conducted and where civilians were casualties?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember well an incident in the B-Phase where a teacher was killed with a certain number of pupils. I think it was the wife of Vehid Gunic in that case, if I am not mistaken. And I know that all of these expert groups worked for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say all the expert groups of the commission worked on it, when you say "expert groups" --

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am thinking of the courts, the civilian police, and also the military security of the general staff and also of the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Specifically regarding this incident that you mentioned, when you received the report about the incident, who did you pass the report on to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually in such cases, my officers were there simply in order to provide information from the corps. The reports were made directly by the commission and they were sent to higher levels. I would be just briefly informed by my officers who participated in this work.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you informed about who these reports were ultimately sent to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They must be sent to the general staff, also to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and to the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karavelic, can you tell us, in the period of 1992 and 1994, how frequent were the battles on the Sarajevo front?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, how frequent were they? They went on nonstop.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "nonstop," that means every day?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, literally, almost literally every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us, in which part of the Sarajevo theatre of war were the most intense battles?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most intense battles in Sarajevo took place, first of all, in Golo Brdo and Zuc, then in Azici and Stupska Petlja. Then third or fourth place would be in Dobrinja or Mojmilo. In the fifth place, the Jewish cemetery, and so on. In the sixth place, the Grdonj Spicasta Stijena area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In those areas, could you please tell us how wide was the line of separation between the warring parties?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the place. In some places, the lines were separated literally by 10 metres on a point 100 -- 850 in Zuc. But in some places, the line was about 100 metres apart.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you please tell us something about the operation "Jug South" conducted by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operation "Jug"? Could you please explain? That doesn't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
