utterances.text: From the month of July until October, was the operation "Jug South" planned and conducted by the army of BH?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I would know it by some other name, but this name doesn't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about from the month of November, Operation Envelope, "Kovera"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell in which area, which region, this action was taken, the Operation Envelope?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the territory of Igman, Bjelasnica, Trnovo and Jahorina. I think that this is it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In which period did this take place? Was that November?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a problem in translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It appears on page 48, line 18, that the answer of the witness on the question on Operation Envelope Koverat would be, "I don't know anything about it," which seems to be inconsistent with his following answers on the other questions. Did you know about the Operation Envelope, "Koverat"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you tell us specifically the period or the duration of the Operation "Envelope"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you the period exactly. I think it was late autumn 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, did you -- do you have any information about the existence of ammunition-producing workshops, also for the repair an maintenance of weapons, specifically in the brewery Pivera, Bistrik?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Pivera in Bistrik. I know about others, but the Bistrik Pivera, I don't know what to say about that. It is possible, possibly yes, probably no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the ones you do know about?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, the Zrak factory and some other places. Weapons were repaired at the Marshal Tito Barracks quite a lot. And about the rest, you would have to ask the specialised industry ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you informed that there was such a workshop in Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, allow me just to consult with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague will complete the cross-examination. I think we still have about one hour left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Approximately, yes. If it could be done in 50 minutes, it would be fine by doing it as efficiently as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I take note and I would like to thank the witness, if he can answer by "yes" or "no," in advance. Mr. President, to start with, we are going to need the assistance Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of Madam Usher and of my colleague, Ms. Pilipovic. Before we do anything, we are going to have to show some maps, please. The first map that we would like to show, we haven't been able to copy it because of its size, but it was organised with the technical booth which is going to show it on the screen. We have only reproduced sections of this map, but we will show it, we will let you have a look at it, and perhaps the witness will be able to indicate things on this map. Thank you. I think we should be able to see it on a screen. I don't know whether this will be possible. Here we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, would you be able to have a look at this map and confirm that this is a headquarters map of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think the question should at least also indicate a date, as of what date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This will come. This will come, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you first -- if we can first identify whether this chart comes from, then the next question might be -- if on the other hand, it would be totally out of the time frame of the indictment period, then, of course, the order perhaps should be different.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, would you, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would it be possible to approach the map to the witness so that he can have a took at what is in the top left hand corner. This is a map that was disclosed to us by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please read the dates that are on the map? Aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beginning of the 1st of December, 1992, ending on the 4th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, is there a stamp on this map, a blue stamp which is showing the coat of arms of the BH army; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, this map, is this a working map? I don't have it before me but I believe that is what it is called, a working map.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states "working map," and in the beginning you said that this was the working map of the general staff or the main staff, but it is actually the working map of the 1st Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So this is a working map of the 1st Corps, that is of the Main Staff of the 1st Corps, right, you identified as such?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is from the archives, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is the first series of the maps, and this map can now be set aside and we are going to go on, unless Mr. Ierace has some problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I enquire through you whether the Defence intends to tender the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you intend to tender the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already answered this question, Mr. President, by saying that we have made copies, partial copies, but first of all, we wanted to show it because we are not able to copy this document which has like three or five square metres of surface. It is outside of the possibilities of the Defence. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... let's try to be practical. What you seek is to establish through this witness that the part you copied are parts of this map, and then tender the smaller copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the reason I rise to my feet is the Prosecution would have appreciated some indication from the Defence that they intended to show the witness the map and photocopies of sections of it. Pursuant to a direction which you gave many months ago, I don't want to waste time but simply state that, in future, could the Defence please be in strict terms required to comply with that direction. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let's have in mind what Mr. Ierace said, that in the future you should strictly follow the rules. Then let's not discuss whether you did it at this moment, and please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Second map, same procedure, please. We can set this map aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We will first ask you, Witness, whether you know the name of Mr. Zlatko Mujezinovic. Do you know the name of this person?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zlatko Mujezinovic. There is a Zlatko and there is a Mujezinovic, but I don't know whether -- in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, but I don't know whether his name is Zlatko.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Again, this map covers the period 10th of March, 1993, end of January 1994. If we can show it, please. Witness, can you read the title, the name of this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, again because I received absolutely no warning, although my friend found time, it seems, to speak to the video unit, perhaps he could be so kind as to assist us by telling us what the map shows, since we can't see it from this distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the exercise you are doing now has taken a lot of preparation. There would have been ample opportunity -- even if the issues would have come up in examination-in-chief, there would have been ample opportunity, seeing what efforts you have to make, to inform the Prosecution. Would you please tell now the Prosecution what this map is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, gladly, although --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask for any comment at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is a map, an army map, which is showing the situation of lines at a given period, that is between the two dates which I have just given you a moment ago. This was the March and January 1993. Now, this map is showing lines of both parties, of both sides, and this is a map of Sarajevo. It should be on the screens. Perhaps it is not well positioned, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the screen does not show the map properly. If he could just tell me, does it show the whole of the city, does it show the entire confrontation lines around the city?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is showing not only the entire city, but more than that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Madam Usher, could you please approach the Prosecution bench to give a better view to the Prosecution on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, and still in order to save time, Mr. President, I would like to just tell Madam Usher that we will -- Madam Registrar, that we will need all the maps in relation to the 27 sniping incidents and the 5 incidents, shelling incidents, that were shown to the witness yesterday so that we can look at them in parallel with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to know whether -- whether Mr. Ierace -- whether Mr. Ierace has anything to say so that we can finish this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Ierace has something to say, he will be on his feet and tell us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. So perhaps we can show the witness -- thank you, Madam Usher, thank you very much. Perhaps we can show the witness very quickly the map that we saw yesterday in relation to incident number one. The reference is 382 and this is Exhibit P3728. In the meantime, we will distribute an exhibit, Mr. President. This exhibit has several copies of the map that we saw earlier, these A-4 copies, in order to make it easier for everyone to read them. Does the witness have the piece 54, the Exhibit 54? May I ask if the Exhibit 154 has been shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that there is some confusion, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. You are asking the map of incident number one, you said. We had two series yesterday, one on shelling incidents, and one on sniping incidents. Was it the sniping one or shelling one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now talking about the sniping incidents, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the reference which I give --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number of the exhibit, Prosecution Exhibit, is 3728.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and which --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Exhibit is 154.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can't follow that last reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which last reference, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last one you gave. You said 154.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I am sorry. The Defence exhibit which we are submitting now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked 154. It should be D153.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Ms. Pilipovic is taking note. Thank you, Madam Registrar. While this document is being distributed, perhaps I should explain, Mr. President, that we have grouped, at the time, the title of the map that we saw with the stamp, and then also the key and also the elements of the map which are in relation to various incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to have a look at page three of this document, please. Do you have it before you? It is in relation to the 1st Motorised Brigade. You can see it to the top right corner. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, the darkest line which is located to the south of the second line, is the line of the Serb forces; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am having some difficulty in following exactly what this page three is, even having re-read the explanation. I take it from the explanation that page three is a portion of the first map that was held up and shown to the witness. Perhaps I could first clarify that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this is a question that is addressed to me, Mr. President, I would answer that this is self-evident. In fact, extremely self-evident. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, there have been two maps shown to the witness, so there is not as such any self evidence in this. But just to clarify the issue --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in the view of the Defence, this is copy made of the first map shown to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have explained the map, the methodology that we are going to use, earlier. I said that the first map, chronologically speaking, is the first one, and now I am furnishing it in copied segments, and I even have the titles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have answered "yes," that would have been enough. Then, please, if it is in dispute, if should be asked to the witness but I don't think, Mr. Ierace, there is any dispute about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There is no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to be precise, that all other elements come from the same map, and the other exhibit will relate to the other map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness -- no, I withdraw that. Is it true that the dark line which is to the south of the other line, to the south of the first line of defence, is the line of the Serb positions; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says on the map. However, this line is not accurate because we can not verify exactly how far the defence line stretches.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am not talking about the stretching of the defence line but I am talking about something else. These lines which are an official map of the headquarters of the corps, is this line, yes or no, a Serb line?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in the beginning that this is how it is on the map. However, the wrong maps were taken from the archives of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, are you saying to us that what is indicated on this map is false, is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here south of the Miljacka river, since the line two or three buildings are not included on the line. It looks as if the Sarajevo Romanija Corps did not hold that line over the Miljacka from the first to the last day of the war. So the entire left bank of the river was held by the Army of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, and whoever drew did this did not do it thoroughly, whoever it was, even if it was me, and it was done superficially.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I have to then consider, Witness, I have to tell you that this line which goes under the river, below the river, is falsely indicated on official maps of the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This official map is not signed by anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But it has a stamp. Could you please answer: It has a military stamp? Could you please answer my question? My question is not to find out whether it has been signed.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on that, it would seem that you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, could you have a look at the line which goes to the east of the stadium, and I am just saying for the parties that the stadium is mentioned -- is located a little bit -- the stadium is this little round form which is located on the -- in the right corner of the left corner. This line, that is below the stadium, is that correctly inputted, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In terms of the translation, I am left a little in the dark --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May me ask the parties now, do we know where the stadium is by now? I know it is a clarification for us. I know it's been a couple of months. Do you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The problem is, Mr. President, the next sentence in the question: "This line that is below the stadium, that is correctly inputted..." I have no idea what line that is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. Could the counsel go a little more slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we just slow down. I think which question, what I understood well was about just part -- one part of the line or several parts separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the second question that I asked was in relation to the line below the stadium, and I can see it - perhaps the others cannot see it - but I can see a dark line which goes along the stadium and then it goes a little bit below the stadium, and then it goes until elevation 648.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: This particular line, has that been correctly inputted, indicated, marked, yes or no? This is a line which is a dotted with long lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is still not correct, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, yes or no? It's still not clear. Let me ask the witness. Do you see the stadium on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is this part here, between two lines. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you see a dark line which starts right from the stadium, turns a bit to the west and then turns south again?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If I could assist, Mr. President, it is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you thinking of this line here that I am pointing to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be zoomed in a bit because I have some difficulties. That is -- now we have north on the top. That line. Is that correctly placed there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next line to the south, could you indicate, that turns to the west. That one, yes. Could it please be moved on the ELMO. Is that line correctly put on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this line wasn't put in correctly either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Next page please, Witness. And we can withdraw the document. Could you please take the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And put it on the ELMO. Could you please assist, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if we can put it on the ELMO, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, we can see here three different types of lines. Is it true to say that the most northern line, the one that appears darkest on the screen, whether it is dotted or not, does this line indicate Serb defence line, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dark black line in the north, yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Now, the middle line, intermediary line, is it true that this is an ulterior position of the defence line of the so-called Sarajevo army positions, that is of the BH army position?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that. I don't know what this intermediate line means.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have the large map back, please, and so that the witness can have a look at it. I just like to be specific -- yes, the original map, which is this one, please, so that the witness can have a look at this area on the original map itself, and by looking at the key which is mentioned on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this map, this should mean that the initial positions that I am showing right now were the positions of the 1st Corps of the BH army, and then this middle line, this thinner line, indicates the advance of the 1st Corps BH army forces. That is what that should mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you please indicate to us what date is connected with the first line you indicated? Yes. So you said the 1st Corps lines, the first you mentioned, I would say the most to the south, what date is related to that, according to the legend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It states here the 1st of December, 1992. And then the line which has been moved forward in these colours, if I can see properly, because I can't tell colours apart very well, it indicates the 14th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. I think that perhaps we can leave the map against the wall, if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will not stand. Perhaps we can just leave it on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, now, looking at the screen now, is it true that there was a considerable advance, an important advance, on the location which is called Mount Grdonj? Could you please show it, indicate it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you please show us where Sedam Suma is on the map, seven woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my learned colleague is not in any way recording what he is showing and not showing so from the transcript. It will not be possible to determine what the evidence actually was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has pointed to the area between the dotted line, the most south of the three, and in the area above it up until the middle dotted line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, just an observation, there is a small triangle which we can see just below the line, and this triangle, is it identifying the highest elevation of the map -- on the mount, as a general rule? If you don't know that, then maybe we can go on to something else.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult to see on this copy whether this part is the highest elevation or this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We could go on to the next page of this exhibit, the one that is showing the region of Kobilja Glava. If it can be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is about all of the incidents that are referring to this rectangle of buildings which appear more or less in the centre, or rather to the right of the map. We can see this rectangle, dark rectangle, and this is a group of buildings that we spoke about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, the line that we have which is dotted, which is to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. north of the map and which goes between Zminjak and Jezerine, is that line -- does this line indicate their positions?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It shows here that, yes, that is so. But I wouldn't recommend this to be considered as an official source of information for several reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you telling me that this is a wrong or a false map?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult to say whether that it is incorrect or that it is false. It is just a matter of -- that it was made by people who were not professionals.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you telling me that the maps of the headquarters of the Main Staff were done by amateurs?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite frequently, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. President, I am just saying for the transcript that this map is in relation to the sniping incident number 4 but also to all the other incidents that are located in the same area that is shown on the map. So in order not to do the same exercise for all of the other incidents because this is the same area on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am going on to the following page, Witness, now. No, in fact, we can abandon this map now because -- we can leave it because the witness said that this -- he wasn't recognising this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I think I would now like the exhibits -- I will just confer, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, the second map that was shown to you, do you consider that this was also a map that was done by nonprofessionals, by amateurs? No, no, do not put anything on the map. Witness, the second map that was shown to you, do you also believe that this map was also made by nonprofessionals?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when you talk about "the other map" when we have approximately 32 maps in front of us, that is not the required position. So you are now referring to the map, second map shown to the witness in the beginning, a large map, black and white. I still do not know the title because it --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a working map, "radna karta." It is a working map just like the other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are referring to that map, and your question was whether that was made by amateurs as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please answer the question, Mr. Karavelic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a working map of the chief of the nuclear biological chemical defence arm branch, and it was part of the 1st Corps. The chief of that section was a person who had -- was not an officer before that. All maps like this which were made by the chiefs of the branches were like this because they were for their own personal use. They were made by them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the question was about whether professionals made these maps or those who lacked the necessary professional qualifications to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that in my previous answer, that this map was made by a person who was not an officer before the war. So he wouldn't know how to mark in certain elements because of his inability to professionally read a map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. President, we are not going to show the other maps that we have prepared with this method, because simply this witness is saying that official maps have been done, have been made by amateurs. So we take note. These are the ones that we have been given by the Prosecution. And I am going on to another line of questioning. I apologise to Madam Usher. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, do what you want to do, but don't bring comments under the disguise of what, in your view, are the conclusions to be drawn from the testimony of the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence is saying this. This is not a personal opinion. It is just saying that it will not present its maps to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I said what you will not do. We will find that. Do what you are going to do. Do not explain why because of your conclusions you would not continue a certain line of question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. Thank you very much. I am proceeding by saying that this is a violation of Articles 20 and 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke of preparation, industrial preparation, in 1991, and you spoke of this in your statement. Do you remember about what you said in your statement; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is it true that starting from 1991, the political structure of Sarajevo is trying to industrially prepare for the war; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was never a part of the political structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What do you mean then by industrial preparation for war?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the preparations after April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am talking about from 1991. These are your words in your statement, Witness.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1991, I was still in the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am asking you, what did you mean by "industrial preparation for the war"? If you cannot answer, please say so.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, and you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, just for the understanding of the Chamber, the line you just confronted the witness with, could you please read it for us so that we know what is the context, so the whole line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that if the witness was unable to tell us what it was about, that he should say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am asking you, just for the understanding of the Chamber, to read the part of the statement that you just confronted the witness with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, indeed. I will find it later, Mr. President. I will read it out later. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said on page six of your statement that there were excellent communications in Sarajevo between the military and the political, the two sides, the military and the political side. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are two statements. Perhaps my friend could just quickly indicate first or second to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly. I am talking about the statement taken the 22nd, 23rd October, 2001, 31st of October 2001, 2nd of November 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please answer, Witness?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was pretty good cooperation, and if I said that, I stand by that, even though my thoughts on that are maybe subjective.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Therefore Witness, in Sarajevo there was, therefore, a certain amount of control of political authorities that they were exercising on the military authorities. Was that the case, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I appreciate you want a minimum of interruptions. But the question was that it was put to the witness that he said in his statement there was excellent communications. The words are: "There was always good communication." I think it is important, in the interest of accuracy, that the adjectives not be overdone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you used a different adjective, would you please then take better care of the text you are quoting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you still answer my question Witness, please?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the question? I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The question was the following: Therefore, there was a political control that was exercised over military authorities?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just -- in the transcript, it is not the same question. But the first question was whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I am constantly being interrupted, it is very hard for me to repeat it word for word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I first let you finish to repeat the question, and then I only noted that, in the first time, your question was about a certain amount of political control, and in your second question there was, at least in the translation that comes to us, political control. Was there a certain amount of political control or was there -- or was there political control?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a little unclear to me what it means, "a certain amount." The army was under the control of the political authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean it was full control? Yes. That's clear. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, were you born in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you live a part of your life in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was exchanged, I entered Sarajevo at that time and I remained there, and I am still living there today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But before, did you live in Sarajevo before?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I am just going to come back to the situation in Sarajevo, and I am saying that the line is 21. And I also said that this was given --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel is speaking far too fast. The interpreters are unable to follow him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you slow down such that the interpreters can follow you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did I understand you well that you are referring to page 10929 and then to 10930?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you indicate the line on the first page that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is line 25 on page 75. This is line 21, 2-1. It is actually marked on the page 75, line 25. I don't know why I always have to be repeating everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have checked page 10929, line 21, and in the English transcript it has nothing to do with this topic. It, therefore, appears that the page reference, if my friend is referring to the English transcript, is incorrect. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you are unable to follow him at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please, at the end of your examination -- cross-examination verify the line taking one minute, perhaps, when there is a re-examination of the witness, and then you will be allowed to give the source. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the source is this one. It appears that there are errors in the pagination, and there is nothing I can do about that. So let us not be asking the impossible. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you are confirming that these weapons never fired at Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier that in the attempt to break through into the town of Sarajevo by the Army of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, we did used to ask for fire from those weapons at -- on Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please answer with a "yes" or "no," Witness. I wanted to know whether these weapons ever fired at Sarajevo; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say, "on Sarajevo"? Where? Sarajevo is a large target.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I didn't say "on Sarajevo," I said "in Sarajevo," from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Into the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness now understands the question and he can answer it. Would you please answer the question whether these weapons fired "from," and I understand "from within Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is not what he asked. The question was, were multiple rocket launchers from Igman, which is far from the city of Sarajevo. It is outside of the Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never asked that, ever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you may now tell me -- I think your question, whether it is a matter of translation or not, but shifted sometimes from firing "at" or firing "from." Do I understand you well that you want to know from this witness whether these weapons fired from within the city of Sarajev?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this was exactly this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that is now the question, Mr. Karavelic. Would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From within the city of Sarajevo, while I was the commander of the 1st Corps, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. That is clear. Does the name of Kazani mean anything to you, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How many -- there were Serbs were killed in Kazani?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can get the answer from the Sarajevo court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Mr. Karavelic, please answer the question. Yes, and do not refer -- if you know, say yes. If you don't know, tell us. Please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I cannot pretend to be telling a greater truth than the truth that I am saying now. There were informations that thousands of Serbs were killed at Kazani. And then information after that came down to a couple of hundred and then afterwards, after court enquiries, and I don't know about that, I don't have any contacts with the courts, is that there weren't even a couple of dozen of victims. The court was in charge of this case. This case arrived here before this Tribunal and then it was sent back to the Sarajevo court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How did these people die?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you know the name of Silos?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the Silos in Tarcin, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was that a detention camp for Serbs?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes. I assume so because I had nothing to do with that camp. It was under the authority of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Does the word Borsalino mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the first time I am hearing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Stela?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that a cafe?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Indeed. Indeed. Is it also a location of a command post, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that is a place in Grbavica near the stadium or the Trg Pere Kosorica Square. I can't place it, but I assume it is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As far as you know, is that also a command post?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the name of Kulin Ban suggest anything to you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in the sense that some smaller units of the HVO perhaps had that name, Kulin Ban, until the Kralj Turtko brigade was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What about Kobra?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As a unit, I don't know where it was, I can't say that, but the name is familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What about the Ljiljan group?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I would like to come back to the question of relief. Is it true --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please explain what he means.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What shifts do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The reserves, the shifts, how did the shifts operate? How did the rotation of shifts operate?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exclusively at night. It couldn't operate at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The shifts, were they done in small groups?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the situation. If the trenches were dug from the city towards the lines, if they were wider, then larger groups could go, so it depended on that. It could be both.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. You stated that the army indirectly were helping the supply of civilians in food and other things?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you be more specific here? If you know that the corps had 45.000 men in the city and in view of the fact that there was no humanitarian aid into the city, it was suspended, and if you also know that a soldier would eat half of his ration and leave a half for his family, then, yes, then it would be possible.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please wait for the translation in English to finish. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are asked to wait until the translation is finished, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, by the interpreters' booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And we don't have the last question at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please repeat the last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I am trying to save time, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know where the kitchens were located in general of the BH army? Were they in the command posts or were they somewhere elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The kitchens were most quite often quite close behind the front line, but it's impossible for me to know all of the places where they were located because there were many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, you said that water was brought to the army in cisterns which were towed by small lorries. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not possible to generalise, because perhaps there were only a couple of cistern trucks in the whole of Sarajevo, mostly this was brought by hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, you said also that it was particularly difficult to distinguish between stray bullets and sniper fire. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, is my friend suggesting this was said in evidence or in a statement? Perhaps he could assist us to that minimum extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am talking about the same statement that we already mentioned on page 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Did you say, sir -- did you state that it was particularly difficult to distinguish the situation when it occurred between a stray bullet and when there was actually sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would be grateful if my friend could read the relevant sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please do so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: "The term sniper is overused, and it is very difficult to prove that an individual has been sniped and not just shot by an ordinary rifle."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shall we just first -- did you finish your reading, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that that would be sufficient, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, quite clearly, the question misrepresented the statement in future --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the future, perhaps, Mr. President, during this cross-examination at least, Mr. Piletta-Zanin could on every occasion read the relevant sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that would be valid for the next three minutes because you have still three minutes to go. Please rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, gladly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: "Is it true that it is very difficult to distinguish between a sniper rifle and an ordinary rifle, which could also be a stray bullet"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, and I am saying again, you would need to examine the victim in order to determine exactly what kind of a bullet it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It is difficult, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Witness, you spoke of mobile mortars and that you also stated that you were never able to find trace --

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So I deduce from your answer, Witness, that in spite of all your organisation, political and military, it was impossible for you in Sarajevo to find out what was happening on some levels of your organisation. Is that correct? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot respond with a yes or a no. You would have to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am very specific. I am talking about mobile mortars, because you were never allegedly able to find the trace of them. So in the organisation, you were never able to control certain levels of your organisation where there was firing?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I believe that they never existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is quite clear, the question is not specific at all. And the witness, I would say, not surprisingly, gives a similar answer, as he did the first time. That whatever his knowledge would have been, certainly hardly any other answer might be possible, I would say, on the basis of the question. It is not a specific question; it is a very general question. You have one minute left, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it true that in spite of all the organisation, military organisation, of the 1st Corps, you were never able to control these mobile mortars, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they never existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, if I tell you, if I put it to you, that there have been many testimonies that mentioned their existence --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That I am not going to quote because I have no time to quote because I only have one minute to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that unfairly represents the evidence. There has been much evidence of suspicion and strong suspicion. It is inaccurate to say, using the words of the question, that there have been many testimonies, implying that there were eyewitnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you put the answer in such a way where it does not provoke the objections, then you might more easily get the answers you are seeking. Would you please rephrase the question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there have been many testimonies that stated that they knew about the existence of mobile mortars that were frequently firing from certain locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If I put it to you that there have been people who have seen these mortars and to whom -- and who were told, "Leave the city immediately for your security," does this mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. That is not the evidence. That phrase related to something entirely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not clear in my recollection. Do you have any specific knowledge, or does it ring a bell to you, that -- or did you ever hear about, whether controlled or not, mobile mortars and what could you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know how many times I received warnings from the UNPROFOR command in Sarajevo in reference to these mobile mortars and also from activities from the areas of the PTT, the Kosevo Hospital, and the State Hospital. Numerous times, I engaged my own police forces at the very moment when they reported this to me from UNPROFOR, so within a few minutes. Because my command post was close to the State Hospital, it is only 200 to 300 metres away. I would have police out on that location within two or three minutes on several occasions, and I never managed to find any of them. Several times I asked the UNPROFOR command to film the incident and also to react and also to inform me. And they never managed to do anything either. I can say that there were mortars, many mortars in Sarajevo. Any brigade had mortars from 60, 62, and 120 millimeters. The fewest of the 120 metres, but my command and my officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it have been possible that someone not under your control would have fired such mortars from those places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are always subversive activities, and elements infiltrated from outside of the town could do it on purpose, to the benefit of the attackers on Sarajevo, if that was useful. But I would not wish to be drawn into something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, one last question and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, but we will not have time to finish. And I would just like us to take note.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you are saying that it is possible that these mobile mortars were infiltrated, that is, taken from the Serb side. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you didn't understand me correctly. Because when I am asked a question whether it was possible that it was somebody else from Sarajevo, and I am expected to answer with a yes or no, I am not able to answer with a yes or no. But if it is somebody from Sarajevo, then I can ask you another question: Why couldn't it be somebody else who entered the city and did it in order to benefit the attackers?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before Mr. Ierace can begin, I would like to clarify the matter, and in order not to waste time, I wanted that when Mr. Ierace tells me this is not what the evidence has shown, this is not what a witness testified, could he perhaps say precisely where this evidence is not correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are referring to evidence previously given in this court, if you are referring to it, it is your task to identify where it is and what it says if the other party challenges the fair representation of that evidence. And we have had many occasions where easily the other party would accept the representation of the evidence given before, but very often we had to experience that it was not well quoted or was a misrepresentation of the evidence, and I think it is also on the basis of this experience that too often the source of the evidence has to be verified, unfortunately. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have something to raise in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karavelic, may I then ask you to just leave the courtroom for one second. I hope it is one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have now had many hours of cross-examination. The Prosecution retained this witness on the witness list, even though it took off some 60 other witnesses. We did so primarily out of the sense of fairness, given that the Defence case is, as I understand it, that the sniping and shelling of civilians, either deliberately or indiscriminately, was perpetrated, at least in a large part, by forces from within the city. I thought it appropriate to retain this witness to make him available for cross-examination so that it could be put to him and the Defence could explore that part of the case. After some hours of cross-examination, it has not been put to him. I draw that to your attention at this stage before I commence my re-examination. I regard it as a matter for the Trial Chamber, as to whether it requires that to be put or whether you are comfortable to simply note it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you have one minute. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I clearly said that after you told me that I would get three minutes, one minute, I said that we would not be able to finish, and I said that we did not finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is the way how you used your time. We resumed at 10 minutes to 2.00 and it is now -- 10 minutes to 1.00 and it is now 25 minutes past 1.00. Madam Usher, could you please bring in the witness again?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before the witness comes in, I do have some questions in re-examination. I don't know whether your Honours have questions. The Hungarian issue does require some immediate, indeed, urgent attention. Although naturally we would not prefer that the witness be here over the weekend, I think you will appreciate when you hear me on the Hungarian issue, that it takes priority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace, I think you can approximately assess how much time you would need. As far as I can see at this moment, there are no questions from the Bench. Yes. Could you please bring in the witness, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked some questions yesterday about Juka's unit or brigade. Could you please clarify whether it was a unit or a brigade --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could Mr. Ierace give me the reference, the page and line, so that I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, Mr. Ierace may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I have no right to find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will tell you if you really can't find it in your computer, but you didn't take the effort to try to do it. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please clarify whether it was a unit or brigade or something else and how many people were in it, approximately.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was formed on paper as a brigade, and that's what it was called, a brigade. I don't believe that it had more than a couple of hundred men, and it was linked to the Main Staff of the Territorial Defence, i.e., the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say it was linked to the Main Staff, was it formally within your command structure? And by "formally" I mean, was it supposed to be part of your command structure or not?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because the zone of responsibility of the 1st Corps, that's where the Main Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was located. So any higher command had the right to link one or two units for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked about 15 minutes ago about when shifts rotated. When did they rotate?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most frequently, in 99 per cent of the time, during the night, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. during bad visibility or during bad weather conditions. During the daytime, only if the weather was bad, if there was fog and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked where were the areas of the most conflict. You mentioned a number of areas in priority. Amongst them was Golo Brdo. Where approximately is that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: West of the Zuc elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Azici?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Azici is between Rajlovac and Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And, finally, Stupska Petlja?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stupska Petlja --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which direction?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- is between -- between the main part of the city and Ilidza, Stupska Petlja. It is crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked a number of questions about the Croatian unit. What was the size of the Croatian unit when it fell under your command and control in 1993? How many men?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a unit that numbered from 500 to 700 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. President, might the witness be shown the document that he handed over just before the morning break. I have translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document he handed over to the Registry, yes. Madam Usher, could you please assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I also have a number of copies of a draft translation of that document. It is a two-page document. They are not stapled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Four copies, unstapled.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, does your signature appear on this document?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received this document on the 9th of May 1992 when I was deported from Sremska Mitrovica to Banjica to Belgrade and then to Pale. And at the same time, I apologise because yesterday I said this was on the 11th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And does the -- who gave you the document?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was given to me personally by the officer in the section which took in and released inmates in the prison service.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does the document in the top left-hand corner indicate anything as to the institution which produced it?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states "collection centre Begejci" and then they cross that out and above it is written legibly "Sremska Mitrovica."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know what happens with this exhibit, but if this exhibit is going to be tendered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you going to tender this?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Defence should be authorised to ask one or two questions in relation to this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would oppose that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is new --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, would you hear me briefly on that? The document was made available to the Defence during cross-examination; it arose directly out of cross-examination. They had ample time to ask questions. They did not need an English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I need an English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why do you need an English translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because there are details that I was perhaps not able to grasp or perhaps a French translation, that would have been nice as well. So that is just a point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may put two short questions in relation to the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness, did you have this document yesterday on you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not here. It was in the -- in my suitcase, in my room, together with some other documents that I have over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No other questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, this means that this concludes your evidence in this court. I thank you very much for having come to The Hague. I know it is quite a distance. You have answered the questions of both parties, and I would like to thank you for that and wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I have a number for this document, please, Mr. Ierac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ierace, I think you asked time, and may I ask you to do it as quickly as possible. First, on the time frame for the Prosecution's case, and second on the Hungarian text.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, yes. For reasons which will become apparent, I ask that I make my submissions on the Hungarian issue in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1.50 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of July, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
